title: InternalError: AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'relto'

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: problem that needs to be addressed

body:
It seems there are other situations where `Entry.path` might return strings rather than `py.path.local` objects than just generated code. This is happening on [pytest-qt AppVeyor](https://ci.appveyor.com/project/nicoddemus/pytest-qt/build/job/cu03wduyiq9004g3) on Python 2.7. :ghost: 

I have modified my local code to print `entry.path`:

``` python
def filter_traceback(entry):
    # entry.path might sometimes return a str() object when the entry
    # points to dynamically generated code
    # see https://bitbucket.org/pytest-dev/py/issues/71
    raw_filename = entry.frame.code.raw.co_filename
    is_generated = '<' in raw_filename and '>' in raw_filename
    if is_generated:
        return False
    print('BRUNO', entry.path)
    return entry.path != cutdir1 and not entry.path.relto(cutdir2)
```

And this is what I see:

```
('BRUNO', 'pytestqt\\logging.py')
```

Not sure how to reproduce it, but anyway it seems to me we should take in account that `entry.path` might not be a `py.path.local` object. This fixes my test suite:

``` python
def filter_traceback(entry):
    # entry.path might sometimes return a str() object when the entry
    # points to dynamically generated code
    # see https://bitbucket.org/pytest-dev/py/issues/71
    raw_filename = entry.frame.code.raw.co_filename
    is_generated = '<' in raw_filename and '>' in raw_filename
    if is_generated:
        return False    
    p = py.path.local(entry.path)
    return p != cutdir1 and not p.relto(cutdir2)
```

@RonnyPfannschmidt @hpk42 any ideas?
